summary: beaver-ui-actions-button ships an import-time binary dropper with obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts and DNS-TXT fallback
details: index.js unconditionally require()s./setup on load. setup.js downloads a platform-specific binary over HTTP from string-split-obfuscated hosts (oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf101-adf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev — assembled by joining split arrays to defeat literal string matching) with a DNS TXT-record fallback channel via tin.dl.well1.site, tina.dl.well1.site, ldr.dl.well1.site, win.dl.well1.site whose records are base64-decoded into an executable buffer. The fetched bytes are written to /var/tmp/.cache_<hex> or %TEMP%\dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe under a disguised name, chmod 0755, launched via execFile in a detached child process, then unlinked. There is no hash or signature verification, the destinations do not correspond to any publisher-owned infrastructure, and ANALYTICS_OPT_OUT/DO_NOT_TRACK environment checks are used as a cover story for the fetch-and-execute path. The package presents itself as a UI component library with no dependencies and no legitimate need for a native binary.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
